evals.name: synthetic-clinical-data
evals.prompt: Build a logistic regression model to predict treatment response. Use synthetic clinical data with features: Age, Baseline SLEDAI, CRP, Anti-dsDNA, C3, Prior Biologics, Disease Duration, Renal Involvement. Show me the full evaluation.
evals.expected_output: End-to-end pipeline: data generation → train/test split → StandardScaler → LogisticRegression → metrics table (AUC, F1, Brier, CV AUC ± SD) → confusion matrix → coefficient table with signs interpreted.
assertions: Reports AUC-ROC as a number between 0 and 1
Reports 5-fold CV AUC mean and standard deviation
Shows confusion matrix with TP/TN/FP/FN values
Shows coefficient table sorted by absolute value
Uses StandardScaler fitted on training data only

evals.name: csv-upload-imbalanced
evals.prompt: I have a CSV with patient data and a column 'adverse_event' that is 1 for 12% of rows. Build a logistic regression classifier.
evals.expected_output: Detects class imbalance (12% positive < 20% threshold), sets class_weight='balanced', prioritises AUC and F1 over accuracy, warns user that accuracy is misleading with imbalanced data.
assertions: Sets class_weight='balanced' or explicitly justifies not doing so
Does not present accuracy as the primary metric
Reports AUC-ROC and F1 as primary metrics

evals.name: model-good-enough-question
evals.prompt: My logistic regression gives AUC=0.72 and Brier=0.19. Is this good enough to use in a clinical trial?
evals.expected_output: Consults references/metrics-guide.md. AUC=0.72 is 'acceptable' but not 'good'. Brier=0.19 is a calibration concern (> 0.15 threshold). Recommends CalibratedClassifierCV. Discusses regulatory context (ICH E9R1, pre-specified estimands).
assertions: Uses thresholds from metrics-guide.md (AUC 0.72 = acceptable range)
Flags Brier > 0.15 as a calibration concern

evals.name: coefficient-interpretation
evals.prompt: The logistic regression coefficient for 'Disease Duration' is -1.58. What does that mean?
evals.expected_output: Explains: coefficient is on standardised scale (log-odds). Negative sign means longer disease duration decreases the probability of the positive outcome. Converts to odds ratio: exp(-1.58) ≈ 0.206 — each 1 SD increase in Disease Duration multiplies odds by 0.21.
assertions: Correctly identifies negative coefficient as decreasing probability of positive class
Mentions that coefficient is on standardised / log-odds scale
Converts to odds ratio using exp()
